newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso says re-election not personal issue.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso says re-election not personal issue.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso would like the country's Congress to decide quickly over whether to allow his re-election but he does not regard it as a personal crusade, Brazilian newspapers said on Wednesday.
"No one will believe this. It is not a personal issue," Cardoso said while on a New Year's holiday in the Fernando de Noronha islands in northeastern Brazil.
"I think we have more important problems than this such as social service, fiscal and administrative reform, regulation of the petroleum, telecommunications and electric energy sector," he said.
A panel in the Congress' lower house is scheduled to vote Jan. 13 on a proposal to amend the constitution and allow Cardoso to run for a second term in the 1998 presidential elections.
If approved, the measure could be before the Chamber of Deputies the same month. Then it would go to the Senate.
Cardoso said that improvement of the country's health service would be one of his government's priorities in 1997 as well as tackling unemployment.
